div.head: I Cn 19.3
div.ab: ⁊ lufige [man] Godes riht heonan forð georne wordes ⁊ dæde: ðonne wurð us eallum Godes milts þe gearuwre.
⁊ lufige man Godes riht henon forð georne wordes ⁊ deda: þonne weorð us eallum Godes miltse þe gearuwre.
⁊ lufie man Godes riht heonan forð georne wordes ⁊ dæde: ðonne wurð us eallum Godes miltse ðe gearwre.
Et Dei iusticiam dictis et factis deinceps amplectamur: tunc eius misericordiam propitiatius impetrabimus.
⁊ lufie man Godes riht heonan forð georne wordes ⁊ dæde; ðonne wurð us eallum Godes miltse ðe gearwre.
And lufige Godes riht heonon forð georne wordes and dæde: ðonne wurð us eallum Godes milts þe gearuwre.
And God's law shall henceforth be zealously cherished in word and in deed; then the mercy of God will be granted the more readily to us all.
And God’s law is to be willingly embraced henceforth in word and deed; then will God show mercy the more readily to us all.
und man (fehlt G) achte hinfort Gottes Gebot sorgsam in Wort und That: dann wird uns allen Gottes Gnade um so bereitwilliger.
and let [people] (lacking in G) eagerly love God's law henceforth in word and deed: then God's mercy will be all the readier for us all.
div.note: ‘man’ supplied in G from B and A. Liebermann compares VI Atr 30.; Robertson (p. 139) takes I Cn from B, which begins at ‘mæssedæg’ in 14.2, the earlier clauses being supplied from G
